newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM denies shielding opposition.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM denies shielding opposition.

text.p: Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh denied on Sunday that he tried to shield the opposition Khmer Nation Party from allegations it took secret funds from the Khmer Rouge.

Ten Cambodians who said they had been undercover Khmer Rouge agents told reporters on Saturday that the pariah Marxist guerrillas sent former finance minister Sam Rainsy $2 million last year to set up the KNP.

Sam Rainsy, who advocates reconciliation with the Khmer Rouge, has not responded to the accusation because he is spending a few weeks as a monk, a custom among Cambodian Buddhists which temporarily bars him from worldly affairs.

Duong Buntha, leader of the group making the charge, said they had first tried to defect to Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC and sought help from Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and his Cambodian People's Party only when turned away by the royalists.

He said the first premier, who has ruled in an uneasy coalition with his former battlefield foe Hun Sen, sent representatives to tell them the time was not right to defect and to keep quiet about Sam Rainsy's alleged ties with the pariah Khmer Rouge.
Ranariddh said on Sunday the story that he had tried to suppress the "defectors'" charges was untrue. "I say very clearly they are lying," he told reporters.
He also expressed doubt about the rest of the story, which was set out at a press conference arranged by Hun Sen's aides.
The accusations against Sam Rainsy has the effect of tarring a potential rival to Hun Sen as a front for the movement whose brutal 1975-79 rule cost more than a million lives.
